verses.sanskrit:
दुर्योधन उवाच।
              न भेतव्यं महाराज न शोच्या भवता वयम्। समर्थाः स्म परान् जेतुं बलिनः समरे विभो ॥१॥
verses.english: Duryodhana said There is nothing to fear, O great king; nor should you grieve for us. We are capable, O king, of winning victory over our battle, O king.

verses.sanskrit: वने प्रव्राजितान् पार्थान् यदाऽऽयान्मधुसूदनः। महता बलचक्रेण परराष्ट्रावमर्दिना ॥२॥
verses.english: When the slayer of Madhu came to the sons of Pritha wandering in exile in the forest with a large army capable of subjugating the kingdom of the enemies and when Kaikeya, Dhrishtaketu, Dhrishtadyumna of the race of Prishata and many other kings followed them to the sons of Pritha.

verses.sanskrit: केकया धृष्टकेतुश्च धृष्टद्युम्नश्व पार्षतः। राजानश्चान्वयुः पार्थान् बहवोऽन्येऽनुयायिनः ॥३॥
verses.bhavadeepa: यदाऽऽयात् आगतस्तदा भीष्मद्रोणकृपाः मया उक्ता इति षष्ठेनान्वयः ॥२॥

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रप्रस्थस्य चादूरात् समाजग्मुर्महारथाः। व्यगर्हयंश्च सङ्गम्य भवन्तं कुरुभिः सह ॥४॥
verses.english: And when not far from Indraprastha there assembled together the car-warriors and having joined together, they blamed you along with the Kurus.

verses.sanskrit: ते युधिष्ठिरमासीनमजिनैः प्रतिवासितम्। कृष्णप्रधानाः संहत्य पर्युपासन्त भारत ॥५॥
verses.english: And when they, with Krishna at their head, paid homage to Yudhishthira, who was wearing deer skin, O Bharata, and when the rulers of men spoke of giving back the duties of a king (to Yudhishthira) and they longed to bring about the overthrow of yourself with all your followers.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यादानं च राज्यस्य कार्यमूचुर्नराधिपाः। भवतः सानुबन्धस्य समुच्छेदं चिकीर्षवः ॥६॥
श्रुत्वा चैवं मयोक्तास्तु भीष्मद्रोणकृपास्तदा। ज्ञातिक्षयभयाद्राजन् भीतेन भरतर्षभ ॥७॥
verses.english: Then were Bhishma, Drona and Kripa thus addressed by me, who heard this, through fear of the ruin of our cousins, Oking, "That the sons of Pandu will abide by the terms agreed to, is my opinion; our destruction does the son of Vasudeva desire.

verses.sanskrit: ततः स्थास्यन्ति समये पाण्डवा इति मे मतिः। समुच्छेदं हि नः कृत्स्नं वासुदेवश्चिकीर्षति ॥८॥
ऋते च विदुरात् सर्वे यूयं वध्या मता मम। धृतराष्ट्रस्तु धर्मज्ञो न वध्यः कुरुसत्तमः ॥९॥
verses.english: That with the exception of Vidura, will you be slain, is my opinion; and Dhritarashtra, who knows the nature of virtue-that best one among the Kurus cannot possibly be slain.

verses.sanskrit: समुच्छेदं च कृत्स्नं नः कृत्वा तात जनार्दनः। एकराज्यं कुरूणां स्म चिकीर्षति युधिष्ठिरे ॥१०॥
verses.english: O dear, having effected our extinction, Janardana desires to bestow on Yudhishthira the entire kingdom of the Kurus.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र किं प्राप्तकालं नः प्रणिपातः पलायनम्। प्राणान् वा संपरित्यज्य प्रतियुध्यामहे परान् ॥११॥
verses.english: When the time comes, what should we do? Surrender or fly or shall we fight against the enemies and give up (all hopes of) our lives.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतियुद्धे तु नियतः स्यादस्माकं पराजयः। युधिष्ठिरस्य सर्वे हि पार्थिवा वशवर्तिनः ॥१२॥
verses.english: In a fight against them, defeat shall surely be ours; all the rulers are on the side of Yudhishthira.
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रणिपातो वा सन्ध्यर्थः । पलायनं वा लज्जयाम् ॥११॥

verses.sanskrit: विरक्तराष्ट्राश्च वयं मित्राणि कुपितानि नः। धिक्कृताः पार्थिवैः सर्वैः स्वजनेन च सर्वशः ॥१३॥
verses.english: On their being dispossessed of their kingdom, our friends are angry with us; and we are reviled by all the kings and by all our kinsmen.

verses.sanskrit: प्रणिपाते न दोषोऽस्ति सन्धिर्नः शाश्वतीः समाः। पितरं त्वेव शोचामि प्रज्ञानेत्रं जनाधिपम् ॥१४॥
verses.english: There is no objection to our surrender; for men or our position seek peace from a long time; but I grieve for my father, that lord of men, who has his wisdom only for his eyes.

verses.sanskrit: मत्कृते दुःखमापन्नं क्लेशं प्राप्तमनन्तकम्। कृतं हि तव पुत्रैश्च परेषामवरोधनम्। मत्प्रियार्थं पुरैवैतद्विदितं ते नरोत्तम ॥१५॥
verses.english: And who may for my doings be beset with troubles and endless woes. The enemies were opposed by your sons simply for our good; which is known to you before, O best among men.
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रणिपाते दोषो वंशक्षयकृतो नास्ति किं तु सन्धिरेव भवति तथापि मम युद्धमेव रोचते इत्याशयेनाह - पितरमिति ॥१४॥

verses.sanskrit: ते राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रस्य सामात्यस्य महारथाः। वैरं प्रतिकरिष्यन्ति कुलोच्छेदेन पाण्डवाः ॥१६॥
verses.english: The sons of Pandu, these mighty carwarriors, will have their revenge for their wrongs by the extinction of the race of the king Dhritarashtra with that of his ministers.
verses.bhavadeepa: हे नरोत्तम धृतराष्ट्र ! तव पुत्रैः अस्माभिः ॥१५॥

verses.sanskrit: ततो द्रोणोऽब्रवीद्भीष्मः कृपो द्रौणिश्च भारत। मत्वा मां महतीं चिन्तामास्थितं व्यथितेन्द्रियम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: Then did Drona and Bhima and Kripa and the son of Drona thus speak, O Bharata, thinking me to be in the midst of great anxiety and with the senses tortured.

verses.sanskrit: अभिद्रुग्धाः परे चेन्नो न भेतव्यं परन्तप। असमर्थाः परे जेतुमस्मान् युधि समास्थितान् ॥१८॥
verses.english: The enemies ready to fight need not be feared, 0 subduer of foes; for the foes when in the battle field are incapable of conquering us.

verses.sanskrit: एकैकशः समर्थाः स्मो विजेतुं सर्वपार्थिवान्। आगच्छन्तु विनेष्यामो दर्पमेषां शितैः शरैः ॥१९॥
verses.english: Each one of us by himself can conquer all the rulers of the earth. Let them come; we shall curb their pride by sharp arrows.
verses.bhavadeepa: नः अस्माभिः परे चेत् यद्यपि अभिदुग्धाः द्रोहविषयं नीताः तथाऽपि न भेतव्यम् ॥१८॥

verses.sanskrit: पुरैकेन हि भीष्मेण विजिताः सर्वपार्थिवाः। मृते पितर्यतिक्रुद्धो रथैनैकेन भारत ॥२०॥
verses.english: In days of old, all the rulers of the earth were conquered by the single Bhima seated on the single car, extremely wrathful on the death of his father.

verses.sanskrit: जघान सुबहूंस्तेषां संरब्धः कुरुसत्तमः। ततस्ते शरणं जग्मुर्देवव्रतमिमं भयात् ॥२१॥
verses.english: That best one among the race of the Kurus, wrathful, killed many among them (enemies); them they out of fear sought the protection of this Devavrata.

verses.sanskrit: स भीष्मः सुसमर्थोऽयमस्माभिः सहितो रणे। परान् विजेतुं तस्मात्ते व्येतु भीर्भरतर्षभ ॥२२॥
verses.english: That Bhishma is well capable to fight along with us and to conquer to enemies; therefore, O bull among the race of Bharata, let your fears be dispelled.

verses.sanskrit: इत्येषां निश्चयो ह्यासीत्तत्कालेऽमिततेजसाम्। पुरा परेषां पृथिवी कृत्स्नाऽऽसीद्वशवर्तिनी ॥२३॥
verses.english: Such was the determination, at that time, of these ones of immeasurable prowess. In days of old the earth was under the possession of the enemies.

verses.sanskrit: अस्मान् पुनरमी नाद्य समर्था जेतुमाहवे। छिन्नपक्षाः परे ह्यद्य वीर्यहीनाश्च पाण्डवाः ॥२४॥
verses.english: Now they are not capable of again conquering us; the Pandavas are now shorn of their wings and devoid of strength.

verses.sanskrit: अस्मत्संस्था च पृथिवी वर्तते भरतर्षभ। एकार्थाः सुखदुःखेषु समानीताश्च पार्थिवाः ॥२५॥
verses.english: The earth, too, O bull among the race of Bharata, is now under our subjection and the rulers of the earth assembled are of the same mind with me in happiness or misery.

verses.sanskrit: अप्यग्निं प्रविशेयुस्ते समुद्रं वा परन्तप। मदर्थं पार्थिवाः सर्वे तद्विद्धि कुरुसत्तम ॥२६॥
verses.english: O subduer of foes, for my sake, the rulers of the earth, can enter into fireor even the ocean; know this, O you best among the race of Kurus.

verses.sanskrit: उन्मत्तमिव चापि त्वां प्रहसन्तीह दुःखितम्। विलपन्तं बहुविधं भीतं परविकत्थने ॥२७॥
verses.english: In this case they laugh at you, who are grieved and like one insane and giving vent to many sorts of lamentations, struck with fear by the descriptions of the enemies.

verses.sanskrit: एषां ह्येकैकशो राज्ञां समर्थः पाण्डवान् प्रति। आत्मानं मन्यते सर्वो व्येतु ते भयमागतम् ॥२८॥
verses.english: Each of these kings by himself are capable of opposing the Pandavas. Every one considers himself all in all. Let the fear which has come on you be dispelled,

verses.sanskrit: जेतुं समग्रां सेनां मे वासवोऽपि न शक्नुयात्। हन्तुमक्षय्यरूपेयं ब्रह्मणोऽपि स्वयंभुवः ॥२९॥
verses.english: To conquer my entire army, which is endless, cannot be annihilated even by Brahma, who is born of himself.

verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिरः पुरं हित्वा पञ्च ग्रामान् स याचति। भीतो हि मामकात् सैन्यात् प्रभावाच्चैव मे विभो ॥३०॥
verses.english: That Yudhishthira foregoing his claims to the entire kingdom begs only five villages; he is afraid of my army and my prowess, O Lord.

verses.sanskrit: समर्थं मन्यसे यच्च कुन्तीपुत्रं वृकोदरम्। तन्मिथ्या न हि मे कृत्स्नं प्रभावं वेत्सि भारत ॥३१॥
verses.english: The impression you have of the might of Vrikodara, the son of Kunti, has no foundation; you do not know my prowess, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: मत्समो हि गदायुद्धे पृथिव्यां नास्ति कश्चन। नासीत् कश्चिदतिक्रान्तो भविता न च कश्चन ॥३२॥
verses.english: My equal in a fight with the mace, there is none in the world; there has been none my equal, nor will there be any.

verses.sanskrit: युक्तो दुःखोषितश्चाहं विद्यापारगतस्तथा। तस्मान्न भीमान्नान्येभ्यो भयं मे विद्यते क्वचित् ॥३३॥
verses.english: Suffering a lot of troubles and employing myself earnestly to my task, have I lived at the abode of my preceptor and learnt my lessons; therefore have I not the slightest fear from Bhima, nor from any other.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनसमो नास्ति गदायामिति निश्चयः। सङ्कर्षणस्य भद्रं ते यत्तदैनमुपावसम् ॥३४॥
verses.english: In a fight with the mace there is none equal to Duryodhana-this is sure; for he used to live with Sankarshana (his preceptor), good betide you.

verses.sanskrit: युद्धे सङ्कर्षणसमो बलेनाभ्यधिको भुवि। गदाप्रहारं भीमो मे न जातु विषहेद्युधि ॥३५॥
verses.english: In a fight I am Sankarshana's equal and in strength there is none my equal in the world; Bhima will not be able to bear the blows of my mace in battle.

verses.sanskrit: एकं प्रहारं यं दद्यां भीमाय रुषितो नृप। स एवैनं नयेद्धोरः क्षिप्रं वैवस्वतक्षयम् ॥३६॥
verses.english: Being enraged, the one blow that I shall deal Bhima, o king, will strike him severely and speedily send him to the palace of death.

verses.sanskrit: इच्छेयं च गदाहस्तं राजन् द्रष्टुं वृकोदरम्। सुचिरं प्रार्थितो ह्येष मम नित्यं मनोरथः ॥३७॥
verses.english: I am desirous, O king, to see Vrikodara with the mace in his hand; this has been prayed for by me for a long time, this has ever been the desire of my heart.

verses.sanskrit: गदया निहतो ह्याजौ मया पार्थो वृकोदरः। विशीर्णगात्रः पृथिवीं परासुः प्रपतिष्यति ॥३८॥
verses.english: Struck by me with the mace, Vrikodara, the son of Pritha, will fall lifeless on the ground with his body smashed.

verses.sanskrit: गदाप्रहाराभिहतो हिमवानपि पर्वतः। सकृन्मया विदीर्येत गिरिः शतसहस्रधा ॥३९॥
verses.english: Struck by a blow from my mace, even the Himavat mountain can be split up into a hundred thousand pieces.

verses.sanskrit: स चाप्येतद्विजानाति वासुदेवार्जुनौ तथा। दुर्योधनसमो नास्ति गदायामिति निश्चयः ॥४०॥
तत्ते वृकोदरमयं भयं व्येतु महाहवे। व्यपनेष्याम्यहं ह्येनं मा राजन् विमना भव ॥४१॥
verses.english: There let your fear proceeding from Vrikodara be dispelled; for I shall kill this one. Do not, O king, yield to grief.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन् मया हते क्षिप्रमर्जुनं बहवो रथाः। तुल्यरूपा विशिष्टाश्च क्षेप्स्यन्ति भरतर्षभ ॥४२॥
verses.english: He being slain by me, many car-warriors, educed with similar qualities, speedily throw down Arjuna, o bull among the race of Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: भीष्मो द्रोणः कृपो द्रौणिः कर्णो भूरिश्रवास्तथा। प्राग्ज्योतिषाधिपः शल्यः सिन्धुराजो जयद्रथः ॥४३॥
verses.english: Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Drona's son and Bhurishrava, Shalya, the king of the Pragjyotish and Jayadratha, the king of the Sindhus,

verses.sanskrit: एकैक एषां शक्तस्तु हन्तुं भारत पाण्डवान्। समेतास्तु क्षणेनैतान्नेष्यन्ति यमसादनम्। समग्रा पार्थिवी सेना पार्थमेकं धनञ्जयम् ॥४४॥
verses.english: Each one of these by himself is competent to kill the Pandavas, O Bharata, Acting together they will in an instant bring them to the abode of death.

verses.sanskrit: कस्मादशक्ता निर्जेतुमिति हेतुर्न विद्यते। शरव्रातैस्तु भीष्मेण शतशो निचितोऽवशः ॥४५॥
verses.english: There is no reason why the entire army of the kings on one side is incapable of conquering the single Dhananjaya. Covered by arrows shot by Bhishma a hundred times.

verses.sanskrit: द्रोणद्रौणिकृपैश्चैव गन्ता पार्थो यमक्षयम्। पितामहोऽपि गाङ्गेयः शान्तनोरधि भारत ॥४६॥
verses.english: And by Drona, his son and Kripa, this son of Pritha will go to the region of the dead. Born of Ganga, our grandfather, too, is superior to the son of Shantanu, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मर्षिसदृशो जज्ञे देवैरपि सुदुःसहः। न हन्ता विद्यते चापि राजन् भीष्मस्य कश्चन ॥४७॥
verses.english: Like a Brahmarshi ( a devotee of the first rank and order) he was born among men and is hard to be vanquished even by the gods. There is no slayer of Bhishma, Oking.

verses.sanskrit: पित्रा ह्युक्तः प्रसन्नेन नाकामस्त्वं मरिष्यसि। ब्रह्मर्षेश्च भरद्वाजाद्द्रोणो द्रोण्यामजायत ॥४८॥
verses.english: This boon was granted by his father who was gratified-'You will not die without your own desire. Drona was born of the Brahmarshi Bharadvaja in a water pot.

verses.sanskrit: द्रोणाज्जज्ञे महाराज द्रौणिश्च परमास्त्रवित्। कृपश्चाचार्यमुख्योऽयं महर्षेर्गौतमादपि ॥४९॥
verses.english: From Drona was born his son, well acquainted with the use of arins. This Kripa, too, is the foremost among the preceptors and was born of the great Rishi Gautama.

verses.sanskrit: शरस्तंबोद्भवः श्रीमानवध्य इति मे मतिः। अयोनिजास्त्रयो ह्येते पिता माता च मातुलः ॥५०॥
verses.english: This one, endued with prosperity and born in a clump of heath, is incapable of being killed, such is my impression. Then, too, the father, mother and maternal uncle of Ashvathaman did not take their birth in a woman's womb.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वत्थाम्नो महाराज स च शूरः स्थितो मम। सर्व एते महाराज देवकल्पा महारथाः ॥५१॥
verses.english: That hero, too, is on my side. All these, o great king, are car-warriors equal to the gods themselves.

verses.sanskrit: शक्रस्यापि व्यथां कुर्युः संयुगे भरतर्षभ। नैतेषामर्जुनः शक्त एकैकं प्रति वीक्षितुम् ॥५२॥
verses.english: They are capable even of giving trouble to Shakra himself in battle. Arjuna is not capable even of gazing at any of them by himself.

verses.sanskrit: सहितास्तु नरव्याघ्रा हनिष्यन्ति धनञ्जयम्। भीष्मद्रोणकृपाणां च तुल्यः कर्णो मतो मम ॥५३॥
verses.english: And these tigers among men united together will kill Dhananjaya. Bhishma, Drona and Kripa together are equal to Karna, such is my opinion.

verses.sanskrit: अनुज्ञातश्च रामेण मत्समोऽसीति भारत। कुण्डले रुचिरे चास्तां कर्णस्य सहजे शुभे ॥५४॥
verses.english: He has been told by Rama-you are equal to me, O Bharata. Two beautiful and blessed ear-rings Karna had from his very birth.

verses.sanskrit: ते शच्यर्थं महेन्द्रेण याचितः स परंतपः। अमोघया महाराज शक्त्या परमभीमया ॥५५॥
verses.english: These two were asked by the great Indra himself for the sake of Sachi, O subduer of foes, in exchange, O great king of greatly terrific strength and infallible.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य शक्त्योपगूढस्य कस्माज्जीवेद्धनञ्जयः। विजयो मे ध्रुवं राजन् फलं पाणाविवाहितम् ॥५६॥
verses.english: How can Dhananjaya escape (after a struggle with) from him who is thus protected; therefore is my victory certain, O king, as a fruit comes within the grasp of my two hands.

verses.sanskrit: अभिव्यक्तः परेषां च कृत्स्नो भुवि पराजयः। अह्ना होकेन भीष्मोऽयं प्रयुतं हन्ति भारत ॥५७॥
verses.english: Our defeat and the success of enemies, too, are proclaimed in the world. In one day this Bhishma kills ten thousand (enemies), 0 Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: तत्समाश्च महेष्वासा द्रोण-द्रौणि-कृपा अपि। संशप्तकानां वृन्दानि क्षत्रियाणां परन्तप ॥५८॥
verses.english: The mighty bowmen, Drona, his son and Kripa, are equal to him (in this respect). Then, too, the ranks of the Sanshaptaka Kshatriya, O subduer of foes, these determined on the destruction of Savyasachin have made this resolution in their mind-Either we shall kill Arjuna or that one having the figure of a monkey on his flag will kill us.

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुनं वयमस्मान् वा निहन्यात् कपिकेतनः। तं चालमिति मन्यन्ते सव्यसाचिवधे धृताः ॥५९॥
पार्थिवाः स भवांस्तेभ्यो ह्यकस्माद्व्यथते कथम्। भीमसेने च निहते कोऽन्यो युध्येत भारत ॥६०॥
verses.english: Such are the kings (on my side); why do you all on a sudden express fear for the enemies. Bhimasena being slain, what other warriors will fight, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: परेषां तन्ममाचक्ष्व यदि वेत्थं परन्तप। पञ्च ते भ्रातरः सर्वे धृष्टद्युम्नोऽथ सात्यकिः ॥६१॥
verses.english: If you know any among the enemies (who will) thus tell me of him, O subduer of enemies. The five brothers along with Dhrishtadyumna and Satyaki these seven warriors whom you consider to be the best among the enemies and the accomplished warriors on our side are Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and others.

verses.sanskrit: परेषां सप्त ये राजन् योधाः सारं बलं मतम्। अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये भीष्मद्रोणकृपादयः ॥६२॥
द्रौणिर्विकर्तनः कर्णः सोमदत्तोऽथ वाल्हिकः। प्राग्ज्योतिषाधिपः शल्य आवन्त्यौ च जयद्रथः ॥६३॥
दुःशासनो दुर्मुखश्च दुःसहश्च विशाम्पते। श्रुतायुश्चित्रसेनश्च पुरुमित्रो विविंशतिः ॥६४॥
verses.english: The son of Drona, Karna, Somadatta, Balhika, Shalya the king of the Pragjyotish, the two kings of Avanti and Jayadratha and Dushasana, Durmukha, Dussaha, O Lord of the world, Shrutayu, Shrutayu, Chitrasena, Purumitra, Vivanshati, Shala, Bhurishravas and Vikarna, your sons. These two can never be equal. Ten and one Akshauhinis have been brought together by me, Oking.

verses.sanskrit: शलो भूरिश्रवाश्चैव विकर्णश्च तवात्मजः। अक्षौहिण्यो हि मे राजन् दशैका च समाहृताः ॥६५॥
न्यूनाः परेषां सप्तैव कस्मान्मे स्यात् पराजयः। बलं त्रिगुणतो हीनं योध्यं प्राह बृहस्पतिः। परेभ्यस्त्रिगुणा चेयं मम राजन्ननीकिनी ॥६६॥
verses.english: That of the enemies is less, it is only seven; why thus should defeat be mine; an army less by a third should be fought with, said Brihaspati. My army, o king, exceeds that of the enemy by a third.

verses.sanskrit: गुणहीनं परेषां च बहु पश्यामि भारत। गुणोदयं बहुगुणमात्मनश्च विशाम्पते ॥६७॥
verses.english: Then again do I see the enemy without any accomplishment, O Bharata; while ours, many accomplishments.

verses.sanskrit: एतत् सर्वं समाज्ञाय बलाग्र्यं मम भारत। न्यूनतां पाण्डवानां च न मोहं गन्तुमर्हसि ॥६८॥
verses.english: O lord, knowing well all this the superiority of my army, O Bharata; and the inferior number of the Pandavas, it is not proper that you should lose your senses.

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा सञ्जयं भूयः पर्यपृच्छत भारत। विवित्सुः प्राप्तकालानि ज्ञात्वा परपुरञ्जयः ॥६९॥
verses.english: Having thus addressed, he asked again of Sanjaya, O Bharata, desirous of knowing more of the enemies thinking that the proper time has come.
